verdict.rationale: Ubuntu's official help and desktop documentation include a 'Get started with the screen reader' guide and a 'Read the screen aloud' page, so a built-in screen reader with onboarding docs exists. However, the evidence consists only of page titles and says nothing about the wider accessibility toolset or whether it works during install and first setup. Missing for 10: evidence of other accessibility tools (magnifier, high contrast, on-screen keyboard), screen reader availability in the installer and first-run setup, details beyond doc headings, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
